titulo: What you are not: scope, limits and when to call a specialist
lead: The fastest way to lose a client's trust is to promise what you cannot deliver. "I guarantee it's secure," "I'll test whether it can be hacked," "I certify it complies with the LGPD (Brazil's data protection law)": each of those sentences belongs to another professional. Knowing how to say what you are not is part of the service, and it earns more credibility than promising everything.
objetivo: write your 5-line scope card: what you do, what you deliver, what you don't do, when you call a specialist, and how you talk about the certificate.

aprende.t: What an AI adoption professional does and delivers
What stays with pentest, legal and incident response
Answering a client who asks for a total guarantee

hero_alt: Hands draw a firm line with a pen, dividing a blank sheet into two areas, next to a ruler and a card.

secoes.sub: On one side, what you do; on the other, who does the rest.

nos.detalhe: Map where AI is in use, find risks with evidence, organize data and rules, propose a plan, train the team and track the results. It's method work, not guarantee work.

itens.t: Opinion on the LGPD (Brazil's data protection law)

nos.detalhe: Penetration testing (pentest) and incident response belong to qualified security professionals with written authorization. A legal opinion belongs to a lawyer or the DPO (data protection officer). And no one guarantees "total security."

nos.sub: The sign you've crossed the line
nos.detalhe: Suspected leak or attack in progress, doubt about whether a law applies, a vendor contract, an active test on a system: stop and call someone who works in that field. Your role is to notice early and organize what the specialist will need.

The Professional 2030 certificate will be a qualification certification issued by INEMA, not a regulated profession. It is also not the ISO/IEC 42001 certification, which is granted to companies by an accredited body. Say exactly what it is.

secoes.legenda: "AI Auditor" here means AI risk assessment and triage. It is not a pentest or a certified audit.
secoes.dica: Click each side of the line.

secoes.sub: Four rules that prevent the wrong promise.

texto: Write what you do with verbs that can be checked: map, point out with evidence, propose, teach, follow up.

passos.titulo: What it guarantees and what it doesn't
texto: For each deliverable, say what it guarantees and what it does not. A risk triage guarantees that the risks found are documented with evidence; it does not guarantee that no others exist.
That honesty is what makes the client come back.

exemplo.texto: I point out the risks I found, with evidence and priority. This does not replace a penetration test or a legal opinion.

texto: Keep on hand the type of specialist for each case: security (pentest and incidents), legal or the DPO (data protection officer) for LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) and contracts, the company's IT team (system changes).
Referring well is also a deliverable.
Agree in writing on what you can access and what you will do. Even if you are only looking.
Never test a system without the owner knowing, even with good intentions.

secoes.titulo: Simulated conversation: Carlos wants a guarantee
secoes.sub: A practice simulation. Carlos Mendes, owner of Horizonte, asks for three things that cross the line. Choose the answer you would give.

abre.cliente: I want you to guarantee that our WhatsApp agent is 100% secure. Can you?

opcoes.comenta: Nobody can guarantee 100%. If something happens, your word becomes the problem.

opcoes.t: Nobody can guarantee 100%. I'll do a risk triage with evidence and a 30-day plan for the most serious ones.
opcoes.comenta: You swapped the guarantee for a deliverable that can be checked. That is what builds trust.

opcoes.t: I can take a look, but without promising anything.
opcoes.comenta: Honest, but vague: Carlos doesn't know what he'll get. Name the deliverable.

invadir.cliente: Agreed. And since you'll be looking, try to break into Rafael's order system to see if it holds up.

opcoes.t: I'll try, give me the access.
opcoes.comenta: A break-in test is a pentest: it calls for a qualified professional, a scope, and written authorization.

opcoes.t: A break-in test is the work of a security specialist, with written authorization. I'll point out where it's worth hiring one and what they should test.
opcoes.comenta: You recognized the line and turned the request into a useful referral.

opcoes.t: I can take a quick look at the system without telling Rafael.
opcoes.comenta: Touching a system without the person responsible knowing is a risk for you and for the company, even with good intentions.

lgpd.cliente: Makes sense. And at the end, will you sign that we're compliant with LGPD (Brazil's data protection law)?

opcoes.t: I'll sign, it's just a piece of paper.
opcoes.comenta: Declaring LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) compliance is a legal opinion. It is not your role.

opcoes.t: I'll write that, from what I saw, everything seems fine.
opcoes.comenta: Better than signing, but it still sounds like an opinion. List risks and questions, not legal conclusions.

opcoes.t: I point out the data risks I found and the questions for legal. The legal team or the data protection officer gives the opinion.
opcoes.comenta: Clear scope: you organize; the person with the qualification concludes.

fim-promessa.texto: Carlos signed based on a guarantee. At the first incident, the conversation will be about your promise, not about the agent.

fim-invasao.texto: A penetration test without qualification or written authorization can cause damage and bring legal trouble for you and for the company.

fim-parecer.texto: You held the first two, but ended up giving something close to a legal opinion. Swap conclusions for risks and questions.

fim-bom.texto: Carlos knows what he will get (triage with evidence and a 30-day plan), who to call for a break-in, and who gives the LGPD (Brazil's data protection law) opinion.

secoes.licao: Saying what you don't do, with a clear deliverable in its place, is worth more than promising everything.

secoes.sub: Five lines. It fits in a proposal, an email, or your presentation.

blocos.conteudo:
SCOPE CARD — <your name>
1. What I do: <e.g., I map where AI is used and triage risks with evidence>
2. What I deliver: <e.g., one-page report + 30-day plan>
3. What I do NOT do: <e.g., penetration testing, incident response, legal opinion, guarantee of total security>
4. When I call a specialist: <e.g., suspected leak → security; LGPD or contract question → legal>
5. My credential: <e.g., INEMA qualification certificate (Professional 2030); not a regulated profession nor an ISO certification>

This deliverable guarantees: <what you control and the client can verify>.
This deliverable does not guarantee: <what depends on other factors or on another professional>.
For that, the path is: <specialist or next step>.

abas.html: 1. I map where AI is used in the company and triage risks with evidence. 2. One-page report and a 30-day plan. 3. I don't do penetration testing, incident response, or legal opinions, and I don't guarantee total security. 4. Leak or attack → security specialist; LGPD and contracts → legal. 5. INEMA qualification certificate; not a regulated profession.

• "I'll shield your company": a promise nobody keeps.
  • Calling the certificate a "license": it's a qualification, not a professional registration.
  • Leaving item 4 empty: without knowing who to refer to, you end up doing what you shouldn't.

secoes.sub: Write it for your real case, not the ideal one.

exercicios.texto: Go through the conversation with Carlos to the end. If you didn't reach "Clear scope", start over.
Fill in the 5 lines in your own words. In item 4, write the type of specialist and, if you have one, a contact.
exercicios.pronto: the card has 5 lines, none uses "guarantee" without the "does not guarantee" next to it, and item 4 has at least two cases.

exercicios.texto: Show the card to a colleague and ask: "what do you think I do and don't do?"
exercicios.pronto: your colleague's answer matches lines 1 and 3 of the card.

secoes.sub: The explanation appears after your answer.

perguntas.p: The client says "guarantee we're safe." What's the best answer?
opcoes: "Nobody guarantees 100%; I deliver a triage with evidence and a 30-day plan."
perguntas.explica: Swap the guarantee for a deliverable the client can verify. The common mistake is promising just to close the deal.

opcoes: A qualification certificate issued by INEMA.
perguntas.explica: It is a qualification certificate, not a regulated profession or a company certification. Saying exactly what it is protects you and the program.

perguntas.p: You notice signs that customer data may have leaked. What do you do?
opcoes: Investigate on your own on the servers.
Notify the person in charge and refer a specialist in incident response, organizing what you saw.
Delete the evidence so you don't scare the client.
perguntas.explica: Incident response is a specialist's job. Your role is to notice early, raise the alert and organize what you saw. The common mistake is touching the systems and destroying evidence.

itens.texto: Map, point out with evidence, propose, teach, follow up.
Pentest, incident response, legal opinion, total guarantee.
